title: The Beauty of Roundabouts
content:

herbst · Sep 14, 2026

The city I grew up in had no roundabouts back then. Today it does have some, some were even made and removed again since. People there hate roundabouts.

The city I live nearby now has so many roundabouts that I can drive for over an hour without seeing a traffic light. It always had those, people are used to using them.

Guess what works better and barely has any traffic issues at all.

LargoLasskhyfv · Sep 14, 2026

As a bicyclist I hate them, at least the smaller ones. Because they slow me down, can't take them with 40 to 50 kph, need to slow down to 30. But that was the intent, yes?

However, crossings with traffic lights I can take at any speed I'm able to, when they are green for me, and I don't need to turn. Or if I can oversee them from afar, and they are empty, and I can give a shit about 'lights'.

herbst · Sep 14, 2026

Some roundabouts here have bike pass troughs on the side (obviously only works if there is no turn to that side) for speedy drivers like you.

Other than that it's obviously by design. There is no reason to speed at constant 50kph in a city. Nether for a car, motorbike or e-bike.

brudgers · Sep 14, 2026

[edit: for clarity, I am not against roundabouts]

I don't have real expertise in civil engineering

Traffic lights have a smaller physical footprint and require less construction activity.

Traffic lights fit on a cost spectrum from two stop sighs, to four stop signs, to stop signs plus blinking lights, to non-trivial signaling.

First make it work. Then make it good. Then make it fast.

Engineering is not a one size fits all discipline.

[edit: I have a background in urban planning, architecture, and real-estate development]
